First, I'll parse the SVG path data:  
- `M 35.02,5.69` — move to starting point.  
- `L 27.03,22.01` — line to (27.03,22.01).  
- `M 27.03,22.01` — move again to same point (so not connected to previous line).  
- `L 25.13,37.49` — line to (25.13,37.49).  
- `L 39.29,41.12` — line to (39.29,41.12).  
- `M 39.29,41.12` — move again.  
- `L 52.79,37.71` — line to (52.79,37.71).  
- `L 35.02,5.69` — line back to start.  

This gives three separate line sequences:  
1. (35.02,5.69) → (27.03,22.01)  
2. (27.03,22.01) → (25.13,37.49) → (39.29,41.12)  
3. (39.29,41.12) → (52.79,37.71) → (35.02,5.69)  

The last segment closes the shape from (52.79,37.71) to (35.02,5.69).  

Counting distinct vertices in order along connected lines:  
- Start at (35.02,5.69) → (27.03,22.01) → (25.13,37.49) → (39.29,41.12) → (52.79,37.71) → back to (35.02,5.69).  

That’s 5 distinct points:  
1. (35.02,5.69)  
2. (27.03,22.01)  
3. (25.13,37.49)  
4. (39.29,41.12)  
5. (52.79,37.71)  

Five vertices → pentagon.  

Final answer: (G)
